study type: secondary analysis of a multicenter randomized controlled trial
exposure: change in HbA1c levels between 14-20 weeks and 24-28 weeks gestation (stable, increasing, or decreasing)
cohort: Obese women diagnosed with gestational diabetes mellitus at 14-20 weeks or 24-28 weeks gestation, who had HbA1c results available.
finding: A single HbA1c measurement in women with GDM was not associated with a composite perinatal adverse outcome, but a stable or increasing HbA1c between 14-20 and 24-28 weeks was associated with an increased frequency of preterm delivery.
mod_finding: A single HbA1c measurement was not significantly associated with primary cesarean delivery, as it was part of the composite outcome which showed no overall association.
cross-section timing: HbA1c measurements were taken at 14-20 weeks and 24-28 weeks gestation.
gest_age: Women were diagnosed with GDM between 14-28 weeks gestation.
